Graduate Admissions
What are the application requirements for a graduate degree in Biomedical Engineering at CU Boulder?
Graduate applicants must hold a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university and have graduated with at least a 3.00 (“B”) grade point average. A candidate who has performed work equivalent to an undergraduate degree or completed 9 semester hours of graduate coursework with a grade point average of 3.25 also meets the minimum requirements for admission. Applicants may also be required to show proof of proficiency in English, which can be done by either attending a qualified institution or submission of an unofficial test score with a Verified Score Report. Full graduate admissions requirements can be found on the University of Colorado Boulder website.
Do I need an engineering degree to be a Biomedical Engineer?
Biomedical Engineering is a highly interdisciplinary field, and we admit students with a variety of diverse backgrounds and skill sets. Suitability for the program is determined after a holistic evaluation of all parts of the application. While students without a strong background in math and science may need to supplement their degree with additional classes, not having a degree in engineering does not disqualify you from our program.
What are the application deadlines for the Biomedical Engineering graduate programs?
For both MS and PhD candidates, the application deadline for Fall 2026 admission is December 1, 2025. Only MS students are eligible to start in the spring semester, and the deadline for Spring 2026 admission is September 1, 2025. Both Spring and Fall semester applications open in mid-July.
What is the application fee for the Biomedical Engineering graduate program?
The application fee for domestic applicants is $50, and the fee for international applicants is $80.
Are application fee waivers available for prospective graduate students?
PhD applicants who are U.S. citizens/PR with a grade point average at least 3.4 will automatically receive an application fee waiver if their application is submitted by November 15 at 11:59pm MST. More info on fee waivers for U.S citizens/PR can be found here.
International applicants may reach out to bme@colorado.edu to request consideration for an application fee waiver after your application is complete and submitted in the online portal. Application fee waivers are very competitive, and their availability varies year to year. To maximize your chance of being awarded an application fee waiver, you should submit your application no later than November 15.
Application fee waivers are not offered to MS applicants.
Do I need to submit letters of recommendation?
Our program requires 3 letters of recommendation, and at least two of your letters must be submitted no later than 10 days after the application deadline. Be sure to give your recommenders sufficient time to write and submit their letters to prevent your application from being withdrawn.
Am I required to submit a GRE score with my application?
GRE scores are not required to apply for our program and are not reviewed during the application review process.
Am I required to submit a WES evaluation with my application?
We do not accept WES evaluations. The University of Colorado Boulder has internal staff that evaluate transcripts, and external evaluations are not required.
How can I prove my proficiency in English?
We require proof of English proficiency from all applicants. Certain applicants may be exempt from submitting exam scores if they meet other conditions as listed on the Graduate School Website, which include citizenship of certain countries or attendance of a qualified institution. Medium of Instruction (MOI) letters are NOT accepted as proof of English proficiency. If you are required to submit a score, “unofficial” test scores are accepted if they are submitted with a Verifiable Score Report.
For students concerned about long wait times or inability to travel to an exam center, our program accepts five different English proficiency tests, some of which are online: TOEFL iBT, IELTS, Duolingo English Test, Pearson PTE, Cambridge English Qualification.
What are my chances of admission?
We cannot provide details about accepted applicant criteria as each application cycle differs greatly. The decision process for each applicant is performed on a case-by-case basis as well as being weighted compared to the applicant pool.
What faculty labs can I work in within the Biomedical Engineering Program?
The Biomedical Engineering Program is a highly interdisciplinary program that draws faculty from several College of Engineering & Applied Science and College of Arts and Science departments. A full list of the research groups affiliated with the Biomedical Engineering Program can be found on our research page and faculty page.
What is the cost of attendance for the Biomedical Engineering graduate programs?
Tuition and fee rate tables can be found on the Tuition and Fee Rate Sheets page on the University Bursar’s website. You can also use the Estimate your Bill tool to calculate the expected cost of attendance. These rates are based on the current academic year’s tuition rates and are subject to change.
How can I fund my graduate education within the Biomedical Engineering Program?
Our PhD program is fully funded, meaning all admitted students will receive a compensation package that includes the cost of tuition, most student fees, and a cost-of-living stipend. Students who continue to make satisfactory progress toward their degree will continue to receive funding for up to 6 years. We still encourage PhD candidates to apply for external sources of funding, such as the NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program, the Draper Scholars Program, the GEM Fellowship Program, and Graduate Fellowships for STEM Diversity.
Our MS program is not a funded program. We recommend that domestic MS applicants apply for FAFSA. MS applicants can also apply for other sources of external funding. This website and this document can be used to search for scholarship opportunities.
How long will my degree last?
MS students have 4 years from the date of enrollment to complete their degree. PhD students are funded for 6 years.
Can I transfer credits from previously completed graduate courses towards my degree?
MS students can transfer up to 9 credits towards their degree from prior graduate certificates, non-degree programs, or incomplete graduate degree programs. No credits can be counted towards your MS degree from a prior completed MS or PhD.
PhD students can transfer up to 21 credits from prior graduate certificates, non-degree programs, completed MS degree programs, or incomplete PhD programs. No credits can be counted toward your PhD degree from a prior completed PhD.
How many credits do I need to take to be classified as “fully enrolled”?
Students enrolled in 5 credits from graduate level courses (5000 - 8000 series) are classified as fully enrolled in a Fall or Spring semester. If you are enrolled in only undergraduate courses (1000 – 4000 series), 12 credits are required per Fall or Spring semester. A student taking a mix of graduate and undergraduate level courses is required to take a total of 8 credits. If enrolled in a Summer semester, the credit requirements are 3 credits if all graduate courses, 6 credits if all undergraduate courses, and 4 credits if a mix of graduate and undergraduate courses. A comprehensive enrollment classification guide can be found on the University Office of the Registrar’s website.
